review_notes: Masaniai safety +1/medium holds. His formation is mixed: prosecution in American Samoa and public defense in Shoreline [S2][S7]. The lean rests on his own statements: 'Justice is about more than punishment' and treatment, job training and community resources to reduce recidivism [S1]. His campaign also lists access to treatment/diversion programs among his priorities [S8], and he has sat on the Mental Health and Veterans therapeutic courts since 2023 [S2]. His explicit readiness to incarcerate repeat offenders [S8] correctly keeps this at +1, not +2. A therapeutic-court assignment is not necessarily his choice, so medium rather than high is right. That matches Martin (West Pos 1, +1/medium on public-defense formation plus Community Court). Masaniai experience -1/high: about five years as a sitting judge, appointed and then elected [S2][S6]. That is a firmer record than Martin's nine months (-1/medium), so the higher confidence is justified. Steinmetz experience 0/medium: his 36-year career, administrative-law-judge and pro tem service and current council seat are all self-reported [S1][S2], and he has no trial-court judgeship. He is scored like Rose-Akins (West Pos 1, 0/medium), a pro tem challenging an incumbent. Omissions are correct. Steinmetz has no bail, diversion or therapeutic-court statements [S1][S2], so safety is properly left blank. Neither candidate gets a judicial score: the _contest.md note filing the CJC reprimand under `judicial` describes judicial conduct, not interpretive philosophy, and the scorer rightly did not score it. No score relies on the 34th LD Democrats' endorsement or the Washington State Democrats' in-kind contribution. Copy flags: (1) Steinmetz's summary and the race_blurb call him a 'former Board of Industrial Insurance Appeals administrative law judge' / 'former administrative law judge' as fact. His dossier says the ALJ role, like the rest of his career, is self-reported and unconfirmed [S2], and the highlight already hedges it ('self-reported'). Suggest 'who reports service as an administrative law judge' in both places. (2) The race_blurb calls Robertson 'Chief Presiding Judge', while this contest's dossiers say 'Chief Judge' [S1]. The title is used elsewhere (SW Pos 5 dossier), so this is cosmetic. (3) The blurb leads with the incumbent's reprimand. That is a tier-1 documented public action [S5] and the central fact of the race, and the sentence also names the challenger's strongest credential, so it reads as neutral.
